Second release candidate of SANKHYA, the LP / MILP / convex QP solver written from scratch for Smart India Hackathon 2026, problem statement SIH26119 (Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd). 161 commits on `main` since v1.0.0-rc1; the version string is now 1.0.0, so the archives are named `sankhya-1.0.0-*`.

## Download

| asset | for |
|---|---|
| `sankhya-1.0.0-linux-x86_64-cpu.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64, glibc 2.35 or later |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-linux-x86_64-cuda.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64 with an NVIDIA driver; the CUDA runtime is linked in |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-windows-x64-cpu.zip` | Windows 10 / 11 x64 |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl` | `pip install` on Linux x86-64, CPython 3.9 to 3.13 |
| `sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-win_amd64.whl` | `pip install` on Windows x64, CPython 3.9 to 3.13 |
| `sankhya-image.tar.gz` | the container image, for `docker load` offline |
| `SHA256SUMS` | over every archive and wheel |

No compiler is needed. Unpack an archive, then from the unpacked directory:

    build/sankhya version
    build/sankhya solve demo/crude_blend.mps --write-sol blend.sol
    python3 tools/verify_solution.py demo/crude_blend.mps blend.sol
    demo/finale.sh                     # Windows: demo\finale.cmd

**Python wheels, new in this release.** The bindings are ctypes over the C API, so one wheel per platform carries the library and the CLI and serves every CPython from 3.9 to 3.13; CI installs each into a clean venv of each of those five versions and solves and verifies the demo there before the draft is made. Nothing is on PyPI; install straight from this release:

    pip install https://github.com/thegoodengineers/SANKHYA/releases/download/v1.0.0-rc2/sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl
    # Windows: .../v1.0.0-rc2/sankhya-1.0.0-py3-none-win_amd64.whl
    python -c "import sankhya; print(sankhya.Model.read('demo/crude_blend.mps').solve().objective)"

Container (CUDA build, the verifier and the demo models):

    docker pull ghcr.io/thegoodengineers/sankhya:v1.0.0-rc2
    docker run --rm --gpus all ghcr.io/thegoodengineers/sankhya:v1.0.0-rc2 sankhya solve demo/crude_blend.mps --gpu

Check a download against `SHA256SUMS`. Each archive's `MANIFEST.txt` records the commit, compiler and CUDA toolkit it was built with and the libraries it links; CI fails the packaging if any of them is an optimization solver.

There is still no Windows CUDA archive. nvcc on Windows needs MSVC as its host compiler and this tree builds with MinGW-w64 GCC; under MSVC 19.44 seven translation units do not compile (the exact arithmetic uses GCC's `__int128` and `__builtin_ctz`, and `src/util/memory.cpp` meets the `min`/`max` macros of `windows.h`). Those need porting first. On Windows, `--gpu` warns and solves on the CPU.

## What changed since rc1

**LP.** Dual steepest edge is the default dual pricing (#860), the hyper-sparse FTRAN and BTRAN are on by default (#878), and the dual's pricing and updates run over the pivot row's support (#849, #877). An LP that reaches no verdict is retried on the model equilibrated by powers of two, then with geometric prescaling at tighter tolerances, with the time that is left (#886, #990). Dual feasibility is judged against the cost and the objective is scaled (#839); presolve keeps every stated coefficient (#824) and restores one basic entry per row (#827). The exact arithmetic now certifies optimal LPs whose float duals prove no bound (#880), repairs a basis that was optimal only to tolerance by exact pivots (#861), with a sparse rational LU (#855). `--iis` names an irreducible infeasible subsystem (#882); the homogeneous self-dual interior point ends an infeasible or unbounded LP with a certificate, behind `ipm_hsd` (#962). Large LPs are routed by the normal-equations bound and the dual's work (#723). `--warm-start previous.sol` re-plans from an earlier basis, survives added and removed rows and columns, and falls back to a cold solve when it cannot prove a verdict (#881, #917, #895); PDHG carries its primal-dual pair into a re-solve (#927, #987).

**MILP.** c-MIR is the default MIR separation (#879); Feasibility Jump is on by default after its A/B (#930, #931); the node LPs after the root price with Devex (#972) and the root is solved by the dual simplex, every node on the time that is left (#817). SOS1, SOS2 and semi-continuous columns are read from MPS and LP and branched natively (#934). Aged cut rows leave the node LP and return when violated (#918). Partial and repaired starting solutions (#944); a relative-gap stop that includes the objective constant (#952). Measured and left off after three-seed A/Bs on `main`: the repeated root cut loop (#957), root restarts and objective branching (#970), conflicts from cutoff nodes (#906). The stats JSON and the MIPLIB CSV now carry probing, clique, conflict and safe-bound counters (#902, #905, #921).

**QP and MIQP.** The QP interior point detects infeasible and unbounded QPs and reports only a certificate the checkers accept (#916); its stall test hands off to the first-order engine (#986) and an active-set finish for complementarity holdouts is behind `qp_ipm_finish` (#988). The convexity test factors Q + shift I and refuses only with a checked negative-curvature witness (#939). MIQP node QPs warm-start from the parent (#924, #960) and get only the time that is left (#945).

**Interior point.** cuDSS by default for large normal equations in cuDSS builds, the CPU factor below the floor (#722); dense columns that cannot fail silently (#936); non-finite answers are never reported converged (#938); every cuDSS call and factorization fallback reads the deadline (#928, #954); the LDL reach is cached at analysis (#923); approximate minimum degree with supervariables, behind an option (#979).

**GPU.** The on-device PDHG loop is on by default (#819). Single-precision inner products with double-precision residuals and refinement, behind `pdhg_precision=mixed` (#984). Feasibility polishing gives a first-order answer primal feasible to 1e-8 with its measured gap (#915). The certified GPU branch and bound was run on an A100 (#926, below).

**New engines, all behind options.** Convex MINLP by outer approximation (`minlp_method=oa`, #976); block-angular detection and Benders decomposition of an LP (#977); a bound certificate for the spatial branch and bound, checked by a tool that never links the solver (#978); engine selection learned from generated LPs (`algorithm_selection=learned`, #941); an optional learned branching policy (#974); a local-model assistant that turns a plain-language request into an LP and solves and verifies it on confirmation (#946).

**Verification and tooling.** The solver and the verifier read the same MPS model: a `$`-led name is a name, only the first RHS, RANGES and BOUNDS vector counts (#964); complementary slackness allows the rounding of its magnitudes in both (#857). The MILP's VIPR proof travels in the evidence bundle and is checked in exact arithmetic on replay (#894). `docs/REPORT.md`, the generated jury report, is checked in CI (#876). The readme opens with a scoreboard generated from the CSVs (#985). `--version` no longer pays for the CUDA probe (#968).

## Measured on main, from the CSVs in bench/results/

- Netlib, all 94 LPs including `truss` and `stocfor3` generated from netlib.org's own bundles, 120 s each, one thread, a 4-core cloud container: `optimal`, within relative 1e-6 of Koch's exact optima and independently verified on **94 of 94**, in each of four runs (`head-to-head-netlib-5e490ef.csv`, `netlib-timing-main-5c15999-r{1,2,3}.csv`).
- Netlib infeasible set, 29 LPs (`netlib-infeasible-5a39fb2.csv`): **28 of 29** certified infeasible with a Farkas certificate the verifier accepts; the 29th ends in `numerical_error`.
- Kennington, 16 LPs at 600 s (`kennington-full-9463fd7.csv`): **16 of 16** match the published optimum and verify, pds-20 included.
- Stress set at `d32b3847` (`stress-d32b3847.csv`, 126 instances at 60 s on a shared laptop): **111 of 126** correct and **0 wrong**; the 15 failures are all time limits, on scaled Netlib (79 of 94 correct there). HiGHS 1.15.1 on the same run and defaults: 29 correct, 90 wrong, 7 failed.
- MIPLIB 3, 52 instances x 3 seeds at 300 s, one thread (`miplib3-300s-seeds3-f2cf240.csv`): **120 of 156** runs reach the published optimum and **113** prove it; HiGHS 1.15.1 on the same container reaches 49 of 52.
- MIPLIB 2017 tier 2, the first 60 benchmark instances with a proven optimum by file size, 3 seeds at 300 s (`miplib-tier2-seeds3-e7c0c60.csv`): **32 of 180** runs reach the optimum and **18** prove it.
- QPLIB, all 453 instances through the reader and the dispatcher at 60 s on the defaults (`qplib-all-8860d2a.csv`): 416 refused with a stated reason (132 non-convex objectives, 284 quadratic constraints without `nonconvex=global`), no reader error, crash or hang; 11 solved and matched, 31 points verified, the 6 the verifier rejects named.
- Certified GPU branch and bound on an A100, 30 MIPLIB instances x 3 seeds at 60 s (`cert-tree-gpu-a100-60-e904ccd.csv`): 27 runs end `optimal`, and **27 of 27** of their GPU-tree proofs are verified exactly by the independent checker.

## Limits, stated

- MIPLIB is the weakest number: on tier 2 most runs end with a verified feasible point and no proof. The harder MIPLIB 2017 instances need better incumbents, not a better bound.
- On the stress set 15 scaled Netlib instances still run out of their 60 s, mostly inside the basis factorization of the scaled attempt.
- PDHG on the GPU wins only above about 5,000 rows on the synthetic ladder and on two of three real instances; below that one CPU thread is faster. On the 779,640-row refinery year every arm still hits the 300 s limit.
- Non-convex QP is refused by default and only bilinear models go to a proven global optimum (`nonconvex=global`); MINLP, Benders and the learned policies are opt-in and measured on small sets only.
- The QP interior point's stall hand-off and the mixed-precision PDHG are new in this candidate and have not been through a full Maros-Meszaros or Netlib re-run on `main` since they merged.
- One wheel per platform, Linux x86-64 and Windows x64 only; no macOS, no aarch64, nothing on PyPI.

The full evidence, including what does not work yet, is in `README.md`, `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` and `docs/NEGATIVE-RESULTS.md` at the tagged commit.
